scope: Live B550 host probe plus three parallel read-only CCR research sweeps over DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash inference engines: the official DeepSeek stack, mainstream frameworks, and niche or overfit ports. The host probe is read-only; no model was started, no download was started or altered, and no engine was built or benchmarked. Worker classifications are research findings, not measurements.

b550_probe.topology: GPU0<->GPU1 PHB (PCIe host bridge), no NVLink
b550_probe.installed_llama_probe: strings on /usr/bin/llama-server found chat-template tokens for deepseek and lfm2 but zero occurrences of deepseek_v41/deepseekv41/DEEPSEEK_V41, and no LLM_ARCH_* tokens; the distro build is CPU-only in practice (no CUDA ggml backend in backends0). It cannot load V4.1.
b550_probe.conclusion: B550 has both 3090 Ti cards effectively idle and 84 GiB RAM available, but no GPU-enabled llama.cpp, no torch, no vLLM, and no SGLang. It has ample storage (20 TiB free on /mnt/weights) and no existing engine that can serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

official_stack.verdict: DeepSeek ships a readable PyTorch+TileLang reference implementation in the model repo's inference/ tree plus four production kernel libraries: FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, TileKernels, DeepSelect. The reference implementation is explicitly not a production engine and has no expert or SSD offload.

niche_and_overfit_ports.target_caveat: The current Hub top entry is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (revision 1bae0e1), a minor update with better agentic scores and top_p 1.0. Support for the original V4.1-Flash may not carry over; any port should pin which of the two it targets.
niche_and_overfit_ports.strata_compatibility: No candidate is byte-compatible with Strata's qwen4exp loader, and none documents the FP4 E2M1 plus UE8M0 and Qwen-shaped kernel contract Strata would need.

locally_moveable_concepts: Expert tiering: VRAM slots over pinned RAM over SSD, per-layer profiles, hit/miss accounting, foresight swap. JigSawPT, Lucebox, and Strata all do this.
SSD-streamed n-gram memory: Strata already streams a 320M-row PLE table; DeepSeek's Engram tables are larger and are disk-mapped by FreeToken, ATOM, WARP, ds4, and atbender.
Host-side n-gram hashing with row gather: identical primitive in Strata's ngram_rows and DeepSeek's NgramHashState.
Grouped top-k expert execution with a shared expert add: same operation; router semantics differ (softmax top-10 vs sqrtsoftplus noaux_tc top-6).
answers_to_the_user_questions.does_strata_support_ssd_streaming: Yes: --mmap-experts, --resident-cpu-experts, --resident-budget-gib, and PleReader's O_DIRECT pread pool.
answers_to_the_user_questions.can_both_fit_in_either_host: Not on Strix (8 GiB VRAM, 91.4 GiB RAM) and not on B550 (2x24 GiB VRAM, 91 GiB RAM, 20 TiB disk) with the published 475 GiB FP4 checkpoint. Both hosts can host the SSD-streaming design; neither has the VRAM or RAM to skip streaming. A 200 GB-class or 128 GB unified-memory box, or a cluster, is where the shipped artifact fits without requantization.

non_claims: No engine was built, started, or benchmarked on B550 or Strix for this task.
The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 transfer on B550 was already running and was not touched; no download was started, resumed, or cancelled.
Worker classifications (native vs fallback, release status, overfit scores) are their reading of upstream source at the cited commits, not measurements.
All performance figures (JigSawPT tok/s, sybil-solutions, ATOM hit rates, vLLM recipes) are third-party published numbers and were not reproduced here.
The actually served worker model per thread could not be tied to a thread id from the router log; the receipt requested_route is not proof of what answered.
